newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm on foreign investor entry.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm on foreign investor entry.

text.p: The Mexican peso reversed early softness to close slightly firmer against the dollar on Thursday due to foreign traders selling dollars to buy Mexican stocks, traders said.
"There was not much volume. It seems they tried to weaken the peso, but it recovered after the Dow and U.S. bonds rallied," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 0.05 and 0.85 of a centavo firmer, respectively at 7.8580/7.8630 and 7.8460/7.8490 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had closed earlier 1.55 centavos weaker at 7.8460/7.8495.
The Mexican bourse was up 41.82 points, or 1.28 percent, at 3,314.98 points as the foreign exchange market was closing.
"The international situation is favorable and traditional year-end demand (for dollars) is low, so the peso is stronger than we were expecting it to be," another trader said.
